$schema_note: Hand-curated record of the numbers ForgePact's drop-rate research already measured, NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file, and hs_game_sdk/drop_roll_model.py never reads it; tests/test_drop_roll_model.py reads both and checks that the model reproduces each entry. The mechanism, in our own words, is docs/models/drop-roll-spec.md. Every entry has `id`, `kind` (`baseline` = vanilla, no lever; `target` = a ForgePact lever applied; `our_code` = a contract of ForgePact's own code, not the game), `status` (`measured`, `qualitative`, `approximate` or `our_code`), `date` (the measurement date; for `our_code` entries, the date the code was read), `source` (a list of {path, section} or {repo, commit}; paths are relative to the hub root, `section` is text that appears in that file), `scripts` (every `gml_Script_*` the entry involves, all bound in hs_game_sdk.scripts.GameScript), `what` (the observation), `model` (what the model must show) and exactly one of `reproduced_by` (the dotted id of the test that reproduces it) or `not_reproduced` (why it cannot be). These rates were all recorded before 2026-09-12, while HookOneScript was still table-only (ForgePact guide, Known Limitations item 12); they are rates per call the hook saw, which is what the gate arithmetic needs. For M2 that holds only if the hook saw every type-12 call to DropDungeonKeys: its denominator counts our own re-calls, its numerator is a table-only hook's counter, which read 95 rather than 0; docs/models/drop-roll-spec.md says what that does and does not establish.

source.section: COZULDU - zindan anahtarlari dogal olarak dusuyor

measurements.what: dungeonkey probe over 200 LoadDrops calls on monsters that drop ordinary keys: type 12 never appeared, and chances[12] was 0 in 200 of 200 calls.
measurements.model: The dungeon-key gate probability is exactly 0 when chances[12] is 0, for any number of die outcomes.

source.section: COZULDU - zindan anahtarlari dogal olarak dusuyor

measurements.what: With dungeonkey on and chance auto, 1233 extra type-12 rolls were made and 95 passed (about 7.7%). chances[11] on those monsters was 5 to 9.
measurements.model: 95/1233 lies inside the binomial band for chances 5 to 9 at the default 100 die outcomes; a forced gate (probability 1) is rejected; the set of die-outcome counts consistent with the observation includes 100.

source.section: COZULDU - zindan anahtarlari dogal olarak dusuyor

measurements.what: 95 DropDungeonKeys calls with every key at its vanilla droprate.base of 1500; the player saw no key.
measurements.model: The probability of no hit in 95 calls is at least 0.5 for an inner scale s of 0.7, 1 and 1/0.7.

source.section: COZULDU - zindan anahtarlari dogal olarak dusuyor

measurements.what: With the key base set to 3, keys became visible.
measurements.model: The expected hits in 95 calls at base 3 are at least 10 for an inner scale s of 0.7, 1 and 1/0.7.

measurements.what: v1.2.1 scaled the relic gate chance by 0.05, and then by 0.001; relics were not reduced (30% and 69% of dropped items).
measurements.model: Gate probabilities are equal for every chance in (0, 1], and the predicted reduction from scale 0.05 to 0.001 is at most 2x, not the intended 50x.

measurements.what: All 156 relics sat at droprate.base 25,000,000, yet relics dropped constantly: DropRelic's drop is not a 1-in-droprate.base roll, so dividing every relic's base by the same factor changed nothing observable. Whether DropRelic reads the base some other way (for example as a weight in the pick between relics) is not established: every relic had the same value, and no run changed a single relic's base.
measurements.model: The relic drop probability does not depend on base, so droprate group relic is a no-op.

measurements.what: The relic share of dropped items. At x2: 30.2% (171/567) before the fix, 6.4% with pre-roll 0.01, 0.7% (1/138) with pre-roll 0.0005. At x100 with pre-roll 0.0005: 5.0% (commit cbac161) or 4.3% (the code comment above g_DkTipOlcek); the two records disagree, so both are kept. Quadratic 0.00025: 0.7% at x2 and 13.5% at x100.
measurements.model: Only the identity 0.00025 x 2^2 = 0.0005 x 2 = 0.001 (the same per-death probability, hence the same 0.7%) and that x100 clamps at 1.
measurements.not_reproduced: A share of dropped items depends on the mix of other items dropped and on kill counts, and neither was recorded, so the model cannot turn a per-death probability into these percentages.

measurements.what: 1.3.10 to 1.3.12 applied the slider to both the gate and the item's own roll (the x50 flood of 2026-09-06, player reports 2026-09-07); 1.3.13 set the gate multiplier to 1 for every family except relic.
measurements.model: With the multiplier applied to both the gate and the roll (both unclamped), the rate relative to x1 is m^2; with the gate multiplier at 1 it is m.

measurements.what: x5 divides the base by five; the vanilla value is stored on first touch; x1 restores it exactly.
measurements.model: 1500 -> 300; a second x5 still gives 300; x1 gives 1500; x5000 floors at 1; the probability ratio is 5 while unclamped.

measurements.what: Karp King was spawned in Act_01_01 1200 px from the hero and killed through its own death path (its protected HP set to 0), 15 times, with every Prime Evil part at its vanilla droprate.base of 27: 11 Karp King's Bellybuttons.
measurements.model: A vanilla boss drops its part, but not on every kill: 11 in 15. Against the x35 run (every roll passes), that is about 0.08 per roll, which puts the inner scale s near 2 for this roll, outside the key rolls' 0.7-1.43.

measurements.what: The same kills with droprate group primeevil x5 (base 27 -> 5.4) and x35 (base 27 -> 1): 36 parts in 12 kills, and 138 parts in 15 kills. A kill rolls the part several times; at x35 one kill dropped up to 14.
measurements.model: Parts per kill scale with the lever until the base floors at 1 (x27 for base 27). The x5/x1 ratio is 5 in the model whatever s is while unclamped. Measured it is 4.1, and its 95% band from the two counts (Poisson log-ratio), 2.1-8.0, contains 5. x35 is saturated, so it gives the most.
